To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA aggregation by polyamine derivatives and their inhibitory effect on DNA relaxation by human topoisomerase 1 are structure dependent.
polyamine-induced DNA aggregation is a prerequisite for top1 catalytic activity.

1) polyamine-induced DNA aggregation is a prerequisite for the top1 inhibition; 2) polyamines with the central (CH(2))12 chain form the best top1 inhibitors; 3) the DNA aggregates formed by the polyamines with the short central (CH(4))10 chain are fluid cholesterics; 4) the polyamines with longer central (CH(3))14 chains form well-structured aggregates that resemble the columnar liquid crystals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of polyamines that can be used for gene delivery or for the design of new top1 inhibitors with potential for anticancer chemotherapy.
the design of polyamines that can be used to control DNA aggregation, cytostatic or anti-topoisomerase activities, and thus to optimize the efficacy of gene therapy and chemotherapy.
the design of new polyamines as inhibitors of top1 and their DNA-aggregation properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polyamines with the central methylene chain of (CH(2))n = 14 are the best inhibitors of human top1.
polyamine-induced DNA aggregation and its structure is a key factor for top1 inhibition.
the top1 inhibitory activity of polyamines correlates with their DNA-aggregation ability and that the structure of polyamines-induced aggregates is crucial for top1 inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polyamines with the central (CH(2))((n-4)) chain (n=10, 14, 18) form DNA aggregates with different structures and that these structures are crucial for top1 activity.
the top1 inhibitory activities are more complex and sensitive to polyamine structures than the DNA aggregation activities.
the DNA aggregation ability of polyamines is an important factor in their top1 inhibitory activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the length of the central chain of polyamines is crucial for their ability to inhibit top1 activity, and that this effect is related to the formation of DNA aggregates with specific structures.
the length of the central methylene chain of polyamines determines both their ability to induce DNA aggregation and their inhibitory activity on human DNA topoisomerases.
the top1 inhibitory activity of polyamines is related to their DNA aggregation ability and to the structure of the formed DNA aggregates.
